title: What If You’re Outgrowing the Person You Love… Spiritually?
paragraphs:
What If You’re Outgrowing the Person You Love… Spiritually?
When Your Hunger for God Deepens, But The One Beside You Stays Still
There’s a quiet tension no one prepares you for.

Not the loud kind of conflict. Not betrayal. Not shouting.
But something more unsettling…

You start praying deeper.
Worship hits differently.
Scripture stops being words and starts cutting into your heart.
And then you look beside you…
…and they’re still the same.

Still distracted.
Still lukewarm.
Still comfortable where you used to be.
And suddenly, you’re asking a question that feels almost sinful to admit:
“God… what if I’m growing… and they’re not?”

You didn’t plan this.
You didn’t ask to outgrow them spiritually.
But here you are.
Torn between love… and longing for more of God.
Scripture doesn’t ignore this tension.

In Amos 3:3, the prophet asks:
“Can two walk together, except they be agreed?”

In Hebrew, it reads:
הֲיֵלְכוּ שְׁנַיִם יַחְדָּו בִּלְתִּי אִם־נוֹעָדוּ (ha-yelchu shnayim yachdav bilti im no’adu)
“Can two walk together unless they have been appointed or aligned together?”

This isn’t just about agreement in opinions.
It’s about alignment in direction.

Because two people can love each other deeply…
and still be walking toward different destinations.
And that’s where it starts to hurt.

You feel it when you’re crying out to God at night…
while they’re scrolling endlessly beside you.

You feel it when conviction hits your spirit…
but they brush it off like it’s nothing.

You feel it when you want to grow…
but they want to stay.
And slowly, silently…
your soul starts feeling alone… even when you’re not.
But here’s where we have to be careful.
Spiritual maturity is not spiritual superiority.
Jesus never called us to look down on people who are still growing.
In Galatians 6:1, Paul writes:

The Greek says:
καταρτίζετε (katartizete) — to mend, to restore, to gently bring back into alignment.

Not to dominate.
Not to shame.
Not to leave immediately.
But to restore… gently.
And yet… there’s another side.

Because staying in a relationship where your growth is constantly hindered…
where your fire for God is slowly being dimmed…
that’s not love either.

In 1 Corinthians 15:33, it says:
“Do not be deceived: evil company corrupts good character.”

The Greek word for corrupt is:
φθείρει (phtheirei) — to decay, to ruin slowly over time.
Not instantly.
Slowly.
Quietly.
Almost unnoticeably… until one day you realise:

You don’t pray like you used to.
You don’t hunger like you used to.
You don’t burn like you used to.
And that’s the danger.

Not that they’re a bad person…
but that they’re pulling you away from becoming who God is calling you to be.
So what do you do?

You don’t rush.
You don’t panic.
You don’t act out of emotion.
You go back to Jesus.
Because He understands this pain.
Even He walked among people who didn’t fully understand Him.
Even He loved deeply… while being spiritually alone.

In John 2:24, it says:
“But Jesus did not entrust Himself to them…”

The Greek word:
ἐπίστευεν (episteuen) — to entrust, to fully commit oneself.
He loved them… but didn’t give them access to parts of Him they couldn’t steward.
That’s wisdom.
Sometimes maturity doesn’t mean leaving immediately.
Sometimes it means loving… without losing yourself.

Praying… without pressuring.
Leading by example… not control.
Setting boundaries… without bitterness.
But sometimes… if there is no growth… no hunger… no movement toward God…
you have to ask a harder question:

“Am I staying because God is calling me…
or because I’m afraid to let go?”
That question exposes everything.
Be honest.

This isn’t about perfection.
This is about direction.
Are they moving toward Christ… even slowly?
Or are they anchored in comfort?
Because the Gospel is not about staying the same.
It’s about transformation.

The Greek word for repentance is:
μετάνοια (metanoia) — a complete change of mind and direction.

If there’s no metanoia…
there’s no movement.

And if there’s no movement…
eventually, there will be distance.
Not just between you and them…
but between you and God.
And that’s the real risk.
So if this is you…
if you’ve been quietly carrying this weight…
feeling guilty for even thinking it…
you’re not alone.
But you do need to be honest.
Not with people first.
With God.

Because He cares more about your soul…
than your relationship status.
And He is not trying to take something from you.
He is trying to lead you into something deeper.
Stronger.
Holier.
More aligned with His purpose.
And sometimes…
that requires letting Him rewrite the story you thought was already set.
Be honest.
Someone else needs to see your honesty.
You’re going to need this reminder again.
And if you’re serious about growing deeper in Christ—about not staying stuck, about becoming spiritually strong no matter what relationships shift around you—
Stay close to truth.
Because this walk is not easy… and you were never meant to do it alone.
And if you feel God pulling you deeper—into real discipleship, real growth, real transformation—
There is more waiting for you.
If this message convicted you, strengthened you, or woke something up in your spirit…
then don’t just move on.
Support what feeds your soul.
Because sometimes supporting the message… is part of living it.
And sometimes sharing the truth… is part of glorifying God.
You’re not crazy for wanting more of Him.
You’re being called.
And not everyone will come with you.
But Jesus will.
Always.
And He is worth everything.
You were never meant to shrink your fire just to keep someone comfortable in their darkness.
